checks: The reflection intersection is compact, convex, and centrally symmetric. A positive measured fiber and its reflected partner give a positive q-dimensional own fiber.

If its projection has interior, symmetry puts j in that interior and hence in the interior of the projection of C. Lifting an extension of the segment from an interior point yields an ambient interior point over j. Thus q=d, and the fiber and projection dimensions add to n+d for E.

If the base affine span A is proper, compactness leaves only finitely many integer bases of C outside A, at positive distance. Openness and approach to y through interior points give a projected ball off a fixed hyperplane through A and strictly inside that distance.

Every hull point with positive ball weight is off the hyperplane. Convexity of distance excludes all integer bases outside A; over A the hull equals E. This proves exact equality of the entire mixed trace.
Reflection gives the centroid and lower bound R/2, with a generic null boundary giving exact local half depth since q>0. Source b90a2673d60a00b3 §7 asserts the same exact contained construction.

overlap.comparison: This predecessor reconstructs positive full-dimensional fibers after an integer base relabeling for a lattice-width reduction. It does not preserve a specified symmetric extraction's full trace within the original containing C, including q<d or null fibers.

readability: The proper-base-span case and the full-dimensional E case account for zero base dimension without a new branch.
review_method: Independent cold read of the exact frozen statement and proof, then source and predecessor comparison and exact arithmetic checks where relevant.
summary: A one-sided interior ball gives a full-dimensional subbody of C with exactly the reflected mixed trace, including any null fibers.
